I loved the original Payback version, saw it in the theater with my mom. I dug the quick humor and snappy dialog, the ruthlessness of the main character, the whole "I just want my 10 grand" thing (or whatever the amount), the violence... it's actually one of my favorite Mel Gibson movies. When I found out there was another version I hunted it down immediately.

Aaaaaand I didn't like it at all. It was too slow, too normal, too derivative in my opinion. It felt like so many other revenge movies, whereas the original felt almost like a parody of those films. It's one of the only times I've actually far preferred the heavily edited and recut versions of a film to the director's cut but I really didn't care for the director's cut at all.

Anyway, the line "Then what good are you?" and the followup action is one of my favorite moments in film badassery ever.
